fact: The territorial administration ministry (MATGLAC) officially launched the re-reading of law 2009-010 on the organisation of civil status on 21 August 2026, with OIF technical and financial support and UNECA technical input; its director of territorial administration said the reform must take in the digitisation of civil status and the interoperability of systems, across the 117 communes created since the law.

MATGLAC opened a three-day technical workshop on 8 September 2026 for the support unit re-reading the 2009 civil status law, with UNECA expertise; a diagnosis of the law's application is to precede a new or amending law.

Togo First reports that the Ministry of Territorial Administration began a review of the 2009 civil registration law at a scoping meeting in Lomé 'last week' (the week of 17-21 August 2026), to reflect decentralisation, the digitalisation of procedures and interoperability between administrative systems, with reform proposals expected before the end of 2026.

fact: WHO's Togo office reports that in 2024 it supported a national diagnostic of the birth and death registration system, which produced a national roadmap for the digitalisation of CRVS and a multisectoral task force to harmonise practice.

Law 2009-010 (art. 2) places civil registration under the joint supervision of the minister for territorial administration and the minister for justice, who organise, run and control it; declarations are received in the communes by mayors or their delegates (art. 5), and communes buy the registers on the ministry's single model (art. 9).

UNDP Togo's annual report for 2024 states that the digital birth registration platform it supported, in its pilot phase at the Golfe 3 town hall, simplified the registration of births and of other civil status acts, which it does not name.
UNDP Togo states that the digital birth registration platform was implemented in its pilot phase at the Golfe 3 town hall in 2024, one commune; no total of communes or offices is given.

UNDP Togo states that it supported the digitalisation of the civil status centres of the 16 communes of the Savanes region in 2024, which it says can now deliver acts in real time and have been trained to use the digital birth registration platform; it does not say they register on it, and gives no national total of communes or centres.

UNDP Togo states that it supported the development, deployment and operation of the digital birth registration platform, and that the birth tele-declaration in Golfe 3 was set up with its technical and financial support, in 2024; no domestic budget line is mentioned.

UNDP Togo states, on a visit of 27 May 2021, that the Kadodo application in the commune of Lacs 1 (Aného) records civil status acts, naming births, deaths and marriages, and gives the mayor a dashboard of statistics; it reports 1,975 births registered in 2020 against 700 in 2019.
UNDP Togo describes the Kadodo application as in use in one commune, Lacs 1, as of 27 May 2021; it gives no number of civil status centres in the commune and no national total.

UNDP Togo states that Kadodo was selected in a 2020 challenge run by its Accelerator Lab and that UNDP supplied the equipment and trained those involved in Lacs 1; no domestic budget line is mentioned.

WHO's SCORE assessment summary for Togo, on data from 2013 to 2018 and updated 15 March 2021, answers the item on whether all civil registration data are exchanged electronically from local to regional and then central offices with 'paper-based system'; it speaks of the exchange of data between offices, not of the entry itself.
